This machine also has no 3D modelling tools installed (no Blender, no Unity), and the page can't load outside 3D files, so I can't drop a real human model into it right now. **How the real game gets real characters** The spec targets Unity, which renders proper 3D models: thousands of shaped polygons, painted textures, a skeleton for animation. These are made outside the engine. Options, from cheapest to best quality: 1. **VRoid Studio** (free, Windows/Mac). You design an anime-style character with sliders: face shape, jaw, eyes, hair, clothes. It exports straight to Unity. It fits the stylised anime-3D look in your spec well. The catch is that VRoid characters tend to look alike unless you customise them heavily. 2. **AI image-to-3D tools** such as Meshy, Tripo or Rodin. You give them a character drawing and get back a textured 3D model in minutes. They're quick for enemies and creatures. Faces and hands usually need cleanup. 3. **A 3D character artist** (freelance) working in Blender or ZBrush. This gives the best and most original result and is what shipped games use for the main hero. Concept art, model and rig for one hero usually cost a few hundred to a few thousand dollars, depending on the artist. 4. **Free Mixamo animations** (Adobe) then cover walking, running, punching and dodging for any of these models, which helps with your physical combat. Phones handle this kind of stylised character easily. Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail run on mid-range phones with this style. **My recommendation** - **Keep this sheet as the design reference:** outfits, colours, energy colours, proportions, the Uren tell, the Orb. It's a guide for whoever makes the real models, not something to ship. - **Eirik and the Orb:** make them in VRoid Studio to start, or hire an artist if you have a budget. These two carry the game visually. - **Kata Sentinel and the sea creature:** an AI image-to-3D tool is fine, since they don't need human faces. - **Code:** I can build all the game code (movement, camera, combat, Meridian View, Ren, the Uren toggle, the open world) using simple stand-in figures. When the real models are ready, they replace the stand-ins without code changes. Two things to decide: 1. Which route for Eirik: VRoid yourself, an AI tool, or an artist? If you pick VRoid, I can give you exact slider and outfit settings that match this sheet. 2. Are these designs (outfit, colours, story details) approved as the reference, even though the faces themselves will come from the real models? If yes, I'll mark Section 7A in the spec and Gate 2 can close.

This spec is the most achievable of the three. Pixel art in Godot runs on this computer, so you don't need a new GPU machine for it. Here's how I'd proceed. ## The verdict **Code: I can build all of it.** Exploration, combat, Meridian View, the Ren exercises, mastery, the Uren disguise, story state, saves, the comic-panel system, and the world split into chunks that load as you move. **Art: this is the real bottleneck, and I shouldn't be the one making it.** The faces showed I can't make art that "looks excellent". The game needs: - **Eirik sprites:** 8-direction walk, run, dodge, punch, kick, guard, hit and death animations, for each of three looks (wedding, after the incident, Uren disguise). - **Portraits** with several expressions for the main characters. - **Comic-panel illustrations:** several dozen at minimum (5 required Prologue scenes and about 5 in Act I, several panels each). - **Tilesets and landmarks** for 9 regions, plus the Ashplains palette change. ## Plan I'll build everything with clearly marked placeholder art (simple sprites, placeholder panels). Every asset loads from a fixed folder and file name, so finished art replaces the placeholders without code changes. Each milestone is playable on desktop and as an Android build. | Milestone | Build-order steps | What you can play | |---|---|---| | **M1 Foundation** | 1–5 | Eirik moving in 8 directions on a phone (joystick plus buttons), camera, a tiled world, punch, kick, dodge and guard against the first enemy | | **M2 Story engine** | 6–10 | Comic-scene system, dialogue, story state, saves. The full Prologue: royal life, the wedding, the Hollow Shard, the rift | | **M3 The world** | 11 | All 9 Venheilheim regions physically connected, the Cradle visible from far away, depth layers, weather | | **M4 Ren** | 12–18 | Aura failure, Meridian View, Circle, Branch, Pulse and Shape, manual Ren combat, mastered flows, Uren disguise | | **M5 Act I journey** | 19–23 | Records, Deeper Ruins, Cradle and prophecy, sea crossing, Ashplains, "FIND MALAKOR" | | **M6 Polish** | 24 | Final art swapped in, VFX, audio, performance | ## Decisions I've made - **GDScript, not C#.** It's Godot's native language, and Android export with C# is still less reliable in Godot 4. - **Low-resolution pixel canvas scaled up in whole steps, landscape orientation.** Pixels stay crisp on any phone. - **On-screen controls on phones** (joystick plus action buttons); in Meridian View you swipe in a direction. W/A/S/D keep working on desktop, as the spec says. - **First enemy: Kata Sentinels**, stone training constructs left by the pioneers. Venheilheim has no inhabitants in the story, so this avoids inventing new canon. It's listed as a proposal. - **Where the story script and this spec differ, I follow the story script**, as the spec says to. The main case: the spec says Eirik's body "accepts" Ren, but the story has him consciously reject it and force it out first. I'll keep that rejection beat. - **Uren disguise is hold-to-activate**, as the spec says. The story has him disguised for the whole sea crossing, which a held button doesn't fit. The sea-crossing mechanics are open in the spec, so I'll leave that unsolved and handle it when building the crossing. ## What you need to do 1. **Install Godot 4.3 or newer** (standard version, not .NET), plus its Android export templates. For phone builds, also install Android Studio. Godot's Android setup guide covers the rest. 2. **Get the art made. This matters most.** My recommendation, best quality per cost: - **Hire a pixel artist** for Eirik's sprites and portraits, and the key landmarks (Cradle, ruins). - **Hire a comic illustrator** for the story panels; they define the game's identity. - **Buy a high-quality tileset** (itch.io has good fantasy packs) as the base for forests, cliffs and water, and have the pixel artist add Venheilheim-specific pieces. - **Use AI image tools only for drafts** to brief the artists, not as final art. Characters drift between images, and the spec rules out generic-looking art. Once Godot is installed, I'll start M1. Until then I can still write the GDScript and folder structure here, but I won't be able to run it.

regarding the frames in the comic how will we ensure that if generated from a model that they will remain consistent??
Response 541 wordsConsistency is the hardest part of model-made comics. It's solved by giving the model fixed references and fix…
Consistency is the hardest part of model-made comics. It's solved by giving the model fixed references and fixed structure for every panel, not by better prompts. Here's how I'd do it for Venheilheim: **1. Lock each character with a reference sheet first.** Before any panel, generate or commission one approved sheet per character: front, three-quarter and side views, a few expressions, and the outfit details. For Eirik that means: - the spiky dark hair silhouette and grey-blue eyes - gold collar trim, epaulettes, aiguillette and circlet - the hexagon-lined cape (wedding) and the patterned capelet (survivor) Every later image is checked against these sheets. Our current character art is the starting point for the costumes. **2. Feed the sheet back into every generation.** Each tool has its own name for this: - **Midjourney:** character reference (`--cref`) and style reference (`--sref`), so the same face and art style carry across images. - **NovelAI / Stable Diffusion:** reference images (Vibe Transfer, IP-Adapter), or better, a small custom model of each character (a **LoRA**) trained on 15–30 approved images of them. That's the most reliable method; their faces and costumes become something the model "knows." - **Image APIs that accept reference images:** attach the sheet to every request. **3. Fix the composition so the model can't improvise it.** This is where our current panels become useful. The 30 placeholder frames already have the right framing, camera angle and character placement. Feeding each one in as a pose/layout guide (ControlNet in Stable Diffusion, or image-to-image elsewhere) makes the new art follow the same staging, so shots stay continuous: Syra always on the right in the vows, Eirik kneeling in the same spot in the aftermath. **4. Use one locked prompt template.** Every panel prompt has the same fixed blocks (style, palette, line weight, character descriptions word for word), and only the "what's happening" part changes. Same model, same settings, same style reference throughout. **5. Keep text and continuity out of the art.** The game already draws all speech bubbles and captions, so the model never has to produce lettering, which it does badly. Story details like the violet jewel appearing only from the vows onward go on a continuity checklist per panel, checked by eye. **6. Expect to curate and fix.** Even with all of the above, roughly 1 in 3–5 generations is usable, and hands, jewellery and small costume details drift. The workflow is to generate several, pick the best, repair faces, hands and trim with inpainting (regenerating just one region), and ideally have an artist do a final cleanup pass on the key panels. **For this project specifically:** - **Main path:** reference sheets, then a LoRA for Eirik and Syra, with our placeholder panels as layout guides. That gives the most consistent result. - **No graphics card here:** this laptop can't train a LoRA, so that step would run on a cloud GPU (a few dollars) or with a paid service. - **Simplest route:** Midjourney with character and style references gets maybe 80% of the consistency with no setup, plus manual fixes. I can prepare the kit any of these routes need: the prompt template, a per-panel prompt list generated from `COMIC_SCRIPT.md`, layout guides exported from the current panels, and a continuity checklist.

Response 323 wordsYes. The project is already set up for it: the Venheilheim island is generated on its own grid and then placed…
Yes. The project is already set up for it: the Venheilheim island is generated on its own grid and then placed into the world map at an offset (`OX, OY` in `tools/gen_world.py`). Any other region can be built the same way and dropped in later. **How to build a region on its own:** - **Separate map:** develop it (the Sunlit Reaches, Solaris, a port, the Ashplains) as its own map, e.g. `game/assets/world/sunlit_map.bin` plus `_meta.json`. It's playable and testable alone; the game already switches maps with `change_map`, like the palace does today. - **Merging later:** a merge step copies its tiles into the world grid at an offset and shifts all its objects, regions and warps by the same amount, the same few lines used for the island. **Rules that keep the merge painless** (I'll follow them and add them to the handoff file): 1. **Local coordinates only:** each region uses its own grid starting at 0,0 and never hard-codes world positions. 2. **Unique ids:** prefix every object, region and warp with its area, e.g. `reaches_wyrms_rest_dock` or `ash_cinder_gate`, so nothing collides. 3. **Water at the edges:** surround each region with sea on any side that will face the Sea of Sundering, so coastlines join cleanly. 4. **Quests point at ids, not pixel positions:** coordinates change when a region moves, ids don't. 5. **Shared assets:** use the same tile codes and prop names, adding new ones to the shared lists rather than redefining them. **If "isolation" also means separate chats or tools working in parallel:** the project has only one git commit, and other tools have overwritten files before (the Duke sprite). I'd commit the current state now and give each line of work its own git branch. Then merging is a normal git merge, plus the map-merge step above, and nothing can silently clobber anything else. Commits stay local; nothing is pushed anywhere. Want me to make that commit and set up the branches?

<pasted_content id="1c8a"> \documentclass[11pt,a4paper]{article} \usepackage[utf8]{inputenc} \usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry} \usepackage{titlesec} \usepackage{enumitem} \usepackage{setspace} \usepackage{booktabs} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{hyperref} \onehalfspacing \titleformat{\section}{\large\bfseries}{\thesection}{1em}{}[\titlerule] \titleformat{\subsection}{\normalsize\bfseries}{\thesubsection}{1em}{} \titleformat{\subsubsection}{\small\bfseries}{\thesubsubsection}{1em}{} \title{\textbf{Project Codex: Narrative Architecture \& Master Story Bible}} \author{Lead Narrative Design Document --- Core Master File} \date{10 October 2026} \begin{document} \maketitle \begin{abstract} This document serves as the master narrative specification and design framework for Project Codex / Venheilheim. It establishes the hidden world mythology, the socio-biological split between Humans and Uren, the hierarchical energy architecture where Aura and Miasma represent preparatory stages prior to Ren, the uncompressed walkthrough for Act I, the full sequence of the Volcanic Cavern in Act II, and the complete narrative trajectory through to the Epilogue. \end{abstract} \tableofcontents \newpage \section{World Mythology: The Hidden Genesis} \subsection{The Cradle, Primordial Ren, and the Preparatory Arts} In the dawn era, on the isolated central landmass of \textbf{Venheilheim}, the ancestral human race emerged around the Primordial Orb[cite: 3]. This cosmic artifact radiated an undifferentiated, unbounded primordial life-force known as \textbf{Ren}[cite: 3]. Directly channeling raw, unattenuated Ren was inherently dangerous: unprepared physical meridians could rupture under its immense frequency. To solve this, the earliest pioneers developed foundational physical conditioning, breath rhythms, and skin filtration techniques: \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5cm] \item \textbf{Aura as the Foundation:} By drawing environmental energy into an abdominal reservoir (the \textbf{Aura Core}), practitioners learned to temper, fortify, and expand their meridian pathways[cite: 2, 3]. Aura was never intended as the final power; it was the essential \textit{preparatory crucible} that conditioned the body to bear the true current of Ren without self-destructing. \item \textbf{The Rare Peak:} Only the most disciplined master pioneers successfully bridged the gap from Aura into true Ren. The vast majority of the population plateaued at Aura, achieving physical fortitude, basic barriers, and martial kinetic force[cite: 3]. \end{itemize} \subsection{The Peripheral Distortion and Miasma} Peripheral populations on the fringes of Venheilheim observed the pioneers' rapid development from afar[cite: 3]. Lacking the generational guidance of the masters, they attempted to mimic the process by forcing raw ambient energy into their bodies without the proper filters[cite: 3]. This crude intake produced an unstable, turbulent frequency: \textbf{Miasma}[cite: 3]. Yet, just as Aura served as the southern preparatory path, Miasma functioned as the northern counterpart: an incomplete, volatile foundation meant to be refined and tempered toward Ren. Because the fringe dwellers lacked the internal katas to bridge that divide, they remained trapped in this caustic baseline[cite: 3]. \subsection{Equal Opportunity, Child Exploitation, and the Broken Trust} To resolve the growing disparity and provide genuine parity across all communities, the pioneers initiated an outreach project: establishing academies to give equal opportunity to everyone, inviting children from the peripheral communities to learn safe, disciplined cultivation from youth. However, beneath the noble banner of equal opportunity, darker transgressions unfolded. Certain pioneers began exploiting peripheral children as research subjects in experimental cultivation trials, using vulnerable youths to test the limits of energy absorption and technique adaptation[cite: 2]. When peripheral leaders discovered this horrific exploitation, their trust was shattered[cite: 2]. Rather than waiting for further harm, radical leaders organized an infiltration to seize the foundational manuals, scrolls, and sacred artifacts by force to protect their people and claim their own sovereignty[cite: 2, 3]. The operation collapsed into open violence: the \textbf{Hollow Shard} and several ancient relics were stolen, and severe bloodshed ensued, claiming the lives of children caught in the conflict[cite: 2, 3]. \subsection{The Mark of the Forsaken and The Sundering} Horrified by the raid and desperate to safeguard their civilization, the master pioneers closed the academies, sealed their scrolls within fortified city walls, and appointed \textbf{Ancient Guardians} over the Primordial Orb[cite: 2, 3]. \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.5cm] \item \textbf{Imposition of the Mark:} Following the thwarted theft, the pioneers drew power from the Orb to impose a collective, hereditary punishment upon the peripheral peoples[cite: 2, 3]. They branded them with the \textbf{Mark of the Forsaken}---twin runic seals seared symmetrically above the outer collarbones[cite: 2, 3]. The Mark permanently locked their circulation into caustic Miasma, preventing them from ever stabilizing their meridians or progressing to Ren, and triggered physiological mutations (crimson skin, horns, and dark veins): they became the \textbf{Uren}[cite: 2, 3]. \item \textbf{The Second Attack:} Branded, cast out, and bodily mutating, the Uren sought the Orb to break their curse and seize its power[cite: 2]. They launched an all-out ambush against the Ancient Guardians upon the sacred dais[cite: 2, 3]. \item \textbf{The Sundering:} In the violent clash between unstable Miasma and refined Aura, the Guardians were killed, and the Primordial Orb overloaded, shattering into \textbf{three true fragments}[cite: 2, 3]. \end{enumerate} The cataclysm cracked the crust of the earth, sundering the realm into \textbf{three distinct geographical zones} separated by the Sea of Sundering[cite: 2]: \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.5cm] \item \textbf{Venheilheim:} The origin cradle at the center, sealed within dense barrier mists that yield only to Ren[cite: 2]. \item \textbf{The Sunlit Reaches:} The fertile southern continent claimed by the surviving pioneer lineage (Modern Humans)[cite: 2]. \item \textbf{The Ashplains of Nul:} The harsh, volcanic northern continent where the branded survivors were exiled (The Uren)[cite: 2]. \end{enumerate} Three true Orb fragments survived: the \textbf{Cradle Fragment} within Venheilheim, the \textbf{Northern Fragment} beneath the Ashplains sustaining environmental Miasma, and the \textbf{Southern Fragment} beneath the Sunlit Reaches sustaining environmental Aura[cite: 2]. \section{World Geography and Maritime Navigation} The world remains a single globe centered around the Sea of Sundering[cite: 2]: \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5cm] \item \textbf{The Ashplains of Nul (North):} Encompasses active volcanoes, magma fissures, and the \textbf{Obsidian Spires} in the west, with \textbf{Cinder Hold} and the ash-covered \textbf{Obsidian Peaks} in the east[cite: 2]. \item \textbf{The Sunlit Reaches (South):} Spans fertile river valleys centered on the capital of \textbf{Solaris}[cite: 2]. Key landmarks include \textbf{Wyrm's Rest}, \textbf{Verdant Watch}, the \textbf{Great Wyvern River}, \textbf{Emerald Valley}, the \textbf{Luminous Citadel}, \textbf{Goldenfield}, the \textbf{Veridian River}, \textbf{Lierdand Valley}, and the \textbf{Sunpeak Range}. \item \textbf{The Sea of Sundering:} The open ocean dividing north and south, hunted by colossal sea serpents[cite: 2]. \item \textbf{Venheilheim (Center):} The origin island sits in the middle of the sea, ringed by perpetual barrier mist that turns back any ship whose crew lacks Ren[cite: 2]. \item \textbf{The Great Crossing Routes:} Maritime travel must circumvent the central mist via two perimeter sea lanes[cite: 2]: \begin{itemize} \item \textit{Western Great Crossing:} Navigates between \textbf{Wyrm's Rest} (south) and the \textbf{Obsidian Spires} (north)[cite: 2]. \item \textit{Eastern Great Crossing:} Navigates between \textbf{Lierdand Valley} (south) and \textbf{Cinder Hold} (north)[cite: 2]. \end{itemize} \end{itemize} \section{The Power Architecture: Evolution and Loss of Ren} \subsection{Systemic Energy Classification} \begin{table}[h] \centering \begin{tabular}{@{}llll@{}} \toprule \textbf{Energy Type} & \textbf{Dominant Wielders} & \textbf{Circulation Profile} & \textbf{Evolutionary Role} \\ \midrule \textbf{Aura} & Humans & Environmental $\rightarrow$ Meridians $\rightarrow$ Aura Core & Preparatory Stage (Southern Path) \\ \textbf{Miasma} & Uren & Mark-distorted circulation & Preparatory Stage (Northern Path) \\ \textbf{Ren} & Ancient Masters / Eirik & Unbounded whole-body current & Culmination and True Pinnacle \\ \bottomrule \end{tabular} \caption{Systemic Classification of Mortal and Primordial Energies} \end{table} \subsection{The Dual Loss of Ren: How Both Races Forgot the Truth} The loss of Ren across both civilizations was a tragic historical inversion where the \textit{stepping stone was mistaken for the summit}: \paragraph{1. The Human Inversion (Aura Mistaken for the Pinnacle):} \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5cm] \item Originally, the Aura Core was developed as an artificial reservoir in the lower abdomen to safely expand, fortify, and toughen meridians[cite: 2]. Once the channels were sufficiently tempered, a practitioner was supposed to transition from the core's reservoir model into the unbounded whole-body current of Ren. \item However, because bridging into Ren demanded extreme meditative discipline, breath mastery, and physical conditioning, only a tiny elite among the early pioneers ever made the transition. The overwhelming majority remained at Aura[cite: 3]. \item Across generations, the methods of crossing from Aura into Ren were forgotten or suppressed[cite: 2]. Society began to view the Aura Core as the ultimate expression of human power[cite: 2]. \item Over centuries of reliance on this abdominal reservoir, human physiology atrophied: if an individual's Aura Core was destroyed, they were considered permanently crippled, having forgotten that meridians could channel energy directly[cite: 2]. \end{itemize} \paragraph{2. The Uren Inversion (Miasma Mistaken for Identity):} \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5cm] \item In the north, Miasma originated as an unrefined, turbulent attempt to condition meridians without proper filters[cite: 3]. In theory, had the fringe populations received proper guidance, Miasma could have been purified, tempered, and evolved into Ren. \item However, the imposition of the \textbf{Mark of the Forsaken} permanently locked their meridians into that caustic baseline, forbidding any progression[cite: 2, 3]. \item Over centuries of isolation in the ash, the memory of Ren was extinguished[cite: 2]. The Uren came to believe that volatile Miasma was their natural, ancestral birthright, entirely unaware that it was merely an arrested, corrupted preparatory state[cite: 2, 3]. \end{itemize} \section{The Royal Relic and Lineage Failsafe} \subsection{The Sealed Heirloom and Sanitized Chronicle} Passed down through generations of Human monarchs, the \textbf{Royal Relic} is an ancient pendant of pale stone and archaic gold worn on a chain beneath the robes of the reigning king[cite: 2]. It opens exclusively to an infusion of \textbf{pure Ren}[cite: 2]. The parchment preserved within the relic contains the official, sanitized version of history written by the pioneer founders[cite: 2]: \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5cm] \item It claims Venheilheim was strictly a civilization of Aura, completely omitting Ren[cite: 2]. \item It asserts that the founders opened their gates in pure benevolence to peripheral children to offer equal opportunity[cite: 2]. \item It records that the peripheral clans repaid this generosity with unprovoked treason, weaponizing their own children to steal the Orb[cite: 2]. \item It describes the imposition of the Mark as righteous justice[cite: 2]. \item It states that the unrepentant Uren attacked a second time, shattering the Orb and leaving themselves stranded in northern ash[cite: 2]. \end{itemize} This account deliberately erases the pioneers' exploitation of children and their cold abandonment of the borderlands[cite: 2]. \subsection{The Lineage Recognition Mechanism} The pioneers built a failsafe mechanism into the Cradle Fragment keyed to their own leadership bloodline[cite: 2]. It activates under one specific condition: when a direct descendant of the pioneer line has had their cultivated energy completely, violently stripped away[cite: 2]. The conscious spiritual presence of the Primordial Orb repurposes this narrow failsafe into a broader quest for world restoration[cite: 2]. \section{The Prophecy of the Altar} Etched into the cracked stone socket of the central altar on Venheilheim lies the ancient binding prophecy[cite: 2, 3]: \begin{quote} \centering \textit{``When two split crowns drown the earth in spite,}\\ \textit{A hollow vessel shall burn at the dawn of light.}\\ \textit{The child of grief, unmade of Aura, unmarred by the Mark,}\\ \textit{Shall walk the cradle and gather the sundered spark.}\\ \textit{To him who wakes the Ren belongs the binding decree:}\\ \textit{To cleanse the scar, to crown the cinder, and to drown the sea.''[cite: 2]} \end{quote} The prophecy foretells the purification of the Mark, the gathering of the three fragments, and the catastrophic armed struggle arising from world restoration[cite: 2]. The chosen catalyst must exist completely outside the mortal constructs of both Aura and Miasma[cite: 2]. \section{Detailed Campaign Narrative Flow} \subsection{Prologue: The Sacrificial Wedding} Twenty years prior, the old Human King defeated a figurehead Uren warlord in battle and later died peacefully of old age[cite: 2]. His son, Eirik, ascends the throne of Solaris[cite: 2]. Eirik prepares to wed Syra, the daughter of a Duke, whom he loves deeply[cite: 2]. The kingdom has no prospective heir[cite: 2]. Eirik wears the sealed Royal Relic beneath his ceremonial tunic[cite: 2]. Malakor, the true hereditary Uren Rey, operates from the shadows[cite: 2]. Having discovered the Northern Fragment beneath the Ashplains, his scheme is to remove the reigning Human King on his wedding day, execute the bride to inflict maximum psychological trauma, leave the Human throne without an heir, and launch an invasion during the ensuing chaos[cite: 2]. The Uren cabal covertly introduced an ancient pioneer relic---\textbf{The Hollow Shard}---into the court disguised as a dowry jewel[cite: 2, 3]. During the vows, Syra's genuine love activates the shard[cite: 2]. It siphons Eirik's entire Aura Core, delivers a psychic message naming Malakor as the true Uren Rey, overloads, and detonates[cite: 2]. Syra is killed instantly, and the Cradle Fragment pulls Eirik into a spatial rift[cite: 2]. Uren warships strike human shores that same night down the Great Crossing routes[cite: 2]. \subsection{Act I: The Cradle of Silence (Venheilheim)} \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5cm] \item \textbf{Awakening \& Vow of Vengeance:} Eirik awakens alone amidst the overgrown ruins of Venheilheim, his hand instinctively clutching the Royal Relic at his chest[cite: 2]. His grief for Syra hardens into consuming wrath against Malakor[cite: 2]. He vows that this island will not become his tomb; he will hunt Malakor down and avenge Syra at any cost[cite: 2]. \item \textbf{First Combat \& Scavenged Steel:} An ancient stone Kata Sentinel awakens in the ruins[cite: 2]. Powerless and without Aura, Eirik scavenges an ancient double-edged runic longsword from the debris[cite: 2]. Faint white runes line its fuller[cite: 2]. Basic sword combat is established: light slashing chains, dodges, guards, parries, and heavy strikes[cite: 2]. \item \textbf{The Broken Core \& Awakening of Ren:} Eirik attempts standard Human Aura circulation[cite: 2]. The flow collapses completely at his lower abdomen: his Aura Core has been obliterated[cite: 2]. Ambient Ren enters his meridians, flowing naturally through his whole-body network without seeking a reservoir[cite: 2]. Unnerved, Eirik consciously purges the foreign energy[cite: 2]. \item \textbf{Ascent to the Cradle Sanctuary:} Eirik reaches the central sanctuary: a dark slate terrace featuring gold mosaics, broken monoliths, hovering stones, and crystal formations[cite: 2]. At its center sits a cracked altar bleeding golden light beneath the rotating rings of the Cradle Fragment[cite: 2]. \item \textbf{The Incarnation of the Orb:} The Primordial Orb's spiritual consciousness manifests as a woman woven of golden radiance[cite: 2]. She remains neutral regarding his thirst for revenge[cite: 2]. She confirms he was summoned by the lineage failsafe and identifies Ren as an unbounded source of power[cite: 2]. \item \textbf{Unsealing the Relic \& Deepening Hatred:} Noticing the heirloom at his chest, the incarnation instructs Eirik to stop rejecting ambient Ren and pour it directly into the relic[cite: 2]. The relic unseals, revealing the sanitized pioneer scroll[cite: 2]. Reading of the unprovoked Uren betrayal and the punitive imposition of the Mark, Eirik's hatred expands from Malakor to the entire Uren race[cite: 2]. The incarnation does not correct his misconceptions[cite: 2]. \item \textbf{The Compass Shard, Ashplains Destination, and Prophecy:} Eirik demands sufficient power to destroy Malakor[cite: 2]. The incarnation points him north to the Ashplains of Nul[cite: 2]. She recites the full Prophecy and bestows upon him a small, dormant \textbf{Resonance Fragment of the Primordial Orb}, instructing him to use it as a divining compass that will glow and react whenever it draws near the hidden Northern Fragment. She warns him that the barrier mist parts only for a wielder of pure Ren; until his training is complete, the island will hold him captive[cite: 2]. \item \textbf{The Subterranean Training Grounds:} At the Sunken Stair, Eirik descends into a vast underground hall carved into bedrock[cite: 2]. He studies \textit{The First Precept of the Hall}: ``A vessel can be broken. A river cannot''[cite: 2]. He undergoes intensive cultivation: \begin{enumerate} \item \textit{Guard and Parry:} Deflecting blows from animated training constructs[cite: 2]. \item \textit{Continuous Circulation:} Cycling Ren through the meridians and muscle tissue without relying on a core ($\text{Ren} \rightarrow \text{Meridians} \rightarrow \text{Body} \rightarrow \text{Meridians}$)[cite: 2]. \item \textit{Meridian Direction:} Routing energy toward specific limbs[cite: 2]. \item \textit{Body Reinforcement and Swordplay:} Infusing the longsword arm with Ren ($\text{Step} \rightarrow \text{Slash} \rightarrow \text{Route Ren} \rightarrow \text{Right Arm} \rightarrow \text{Reinforce} \rightarrow \text{Release}$), lighting white energy veins along his skin[cite: 2]. \item \textit{Advanced Synthesis:} Combining sword combos with directional Ren bursts[cite: 2]. \end{enumerate} \item \textbf{The Ren Mask (Uren Disguise) \& The Alcohol Warning:} Following his combat training, the incarnation instructs Eirik in using Ren to alter his physical form[cite: 2]. Utilizing his knowledge of Uren anatomy, he shifts his skin to crimson, manifests brow horns, and creates illusory collarbone marks[cite: 2]. The incarnation delivers a critical warning: \textbf{the disguise requires absolute, unbroken conscious concentration; consuming alcohol will dull his mental focus and cause the illusion to instantly shatter}[cite: 2]. \item \textbf{Ship Construction \& The Sea Crossing:} Eirik gathers timber and salvaged iron fittings from abandoned settlements, constructing a vessel at the northern slipway[cite: 2]. He sails into the barrier mist, passing through because he channels Ren[cite: 2]. In the open Sea of Sundering, he battles hostile marine beasts until a colossal sea monster crushes his vessel[cite: 2]. Eirik drifts unconscious atop broken timbers, closing Act I as Commander Vanya's warship approaches[cite: 2]. \end{itemize} \subsection{Act II: The Ash-Choked Shore \& The Flight to the Volcanoes} \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5cm] \item \textbf{Vanya's Conviction \& Disgrace:} Commander Vanya leads a respected battalion in the Uren army. Pragmatic, honor-bound, and fiercely protective of her soldiers, she opposes Malakor's invasion of the Sunlit Reaches, arguing that resources must be spent relieving squalor, famine, and bodily sickness at home. When she voices these convictions to her comrades at sea, Malakor strips her of frontline deployment and banishes her battalion back to the Ashplains in disgrace. \item \textbf{The Rescue of the Disguised Survivor:} Navigating back across the Sea of Sundering, Vanya's crew spots floating wreckage in the water. Clinging to the shattered timbers is Eirik, currently maintaining his crimson-skinned, horned Uren disguise. When pulled aboard and questioned, Eirik stutters and conceals his true royal identity, giving the false commoner alias \textbf{``Torin''}. Despite crew reluctance to waste provisions on an unknown drifter, Vanya refuses to leave a fellow Uren to drown in the freezing currents. \item \textbf{The Voyage to the Obsidian Spires:} On the journey back to the northern coastline, the warship is attacked repeatedly by rogue oceanic predators and mutated sea beasts. Eirik draws his runic blade, fighting alongside the battalion and saving several soldiers from certain death. While his combat effectiveness earns the reluctant respect of some comrades, others grow deeply resentful: \begin{itemize} \item Eirik displays an alien, highly refined martial discipline and growth rate that baffles veteran soldiers. \item During nightly victory celebrations on the deck, Eirik repeatedly and adamantly refuses all alcohol, raising suspicions of aloof arrogance. \item Jealous soldiers constantly complain to Vanya regarding the stranger's unorthodox fighting methods, rapid growth rate, and distant demeanor. \end{itemize} \item \textbf{Arrival at the Obsidian Spires \& Resonance Search:} The battalion docks at the jagged coastal fortress-city of the \textbf{Obsidian Spires}. Vanya secures temporary soldier quarters for Eirik within the military barracks. Guided by the instructions of the Cradle's incarnation, Eirik uses his downtime to scour the smoke-choked streets of the city. He carries the hidden \textbf{Resonance Fragment} beneath his garments, tracking its subtle luminescence and vibrational pulses through city alleys, military foundries, and basalt monuments to detect traces of the Northern Fragment. \item \textbf{The Quarters Confrontation \& Broken Disguise:} Following an exhaustive search, Eirik returns to his assigned quarters to rest. Shortly thereafter, Vanya barges into his room heavily intoxicated, burdened by the bitter humiliation of her demotion and the uncertain future of her soldiers. After guarded conversation where both reveal fragments of their inner exhaustion, Vanya produces a flask of potent northern liquor and insists on sharing a drink as comrades: \begin{itemize} \item \textit{If the player accepts:} Eirik drinks the liquor. The alcohol immediately clouds his mental focus; his Ren flow fractures, his horns dissolve into motes of light, and his crimson skin bleeds away, exposing his fair human face. \item \textit{If the player refuses:} Eirik adamantly rejects the drink. Vanya, stubbornly offended and aggressively playful in her drunkenness, forcibly forces the flask to his lips. The alcohol enters his bloodstream regardless, breaking his concentration and dissolving the disguise before her eyes. \end{itemize} \item \textbf{The Incursion, Accusation, and Stable Flight:} At that exact moment, suspicious soldiers from Vanya’s battalion enter the room to air their ongoing grievances regarding Eirik. Finding their disgraced commander alone with a pale-skinned Human royal, the prejudiced soldiers instantly conclude that Vanya has committed treason by harboring an enemy infiltrator. Shouting alarms and raising their weapons, the soldiers attack both of them. Realizing that explanations are impossible, Vanya and Eirik fight their way out of the barracks, breach the military stables, commandeer mounts, and gallop out of the city gates into the night, fleeing eastward toward the treacherous \textbf{Volcanoes}. \item \textbf{The Volcanic Ride and the Confrontation:} \begin{itemize} \item The player actively controls the mount, riding alongside Vanya across scorched volcanic fields, navigating active lava fissures and evading pursuit scouts. \item Reaching a secluded volcanic ridge, a heated argument breaks out. Vanya demands to know the stranger's real identity, challenging the validity of his alias ``Torin.'' \item Caught in his own lie, Eirik stutters under pressure and finally confesses the truth: he is \textbf{King Eirik of Solaris}. \item Shocked and betrayed, Vanya draws her curved obsidian blade, pressing the steel directly against his throat, demanding to know why the reigning Human monarch is infiltrating Uren lands. \item Before Eirik can explain, the unstable volcanic crust fractures beneath their feet. The ground collapses completely, plunging them both into a deep subterranean cavern. \end{itemize} \item \textbf{The Subterranean Cavern and Ancient Uren Engravings:} Deep within the underground chamber, ancient wall engravings reveal the unredacted history from the Uren perspective: \begin{itemize} \item The engravings show that while the pioneer academies were originally opened under the ideal of providing equal opportunity for all, pioneer researchers secretly exploited peripheral children in dangerous experimental cultivation trials. \item They reveal that the subsequent attack to seize the manuals was a desperate bid by peripheral leaders to stop this exploitation and reclaim their children. \item They document that following this altercation, pioneer masters drew power from the Orb to brand them with the hereditary Mark of the Forsaken, forcibly mutating them into the Uren. \item The carvings depict the second attack on the sacred dais: branded and abandoned, the Uren attacked the Orb to steal it and break their agonizing curse, which resulted in the death of the Guardians and the shattering of the Primordial Orb into fragments. \end{itemize} Confronted with the physical records of his ancestors' child exploitation and betrayal, Eirik's inherited hatred begins to crack. \end{itemize} \subsection{Act III: The Burning Capital (The Sunlit Reaches)} \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5cm] \item \textbf{Return to the Southern Continent:} Eirik and Vanya navigate south to the Sunlit Reaches via the Great Crossing maritime routes. \item \textbf{Human Religious Tyranny:} In Solaris, Arch-Inquisitor Vael and the Royal Inquisition have exploited Eirik's disappearance and the coastal war to seize absolute authority. The religious hierarchy secretly taps the Southern Fragment's Aura to consolidate power, while Vael institutes martial law and conducts brutal purges against citizens suspected of carrying Uren blood. Vael harnesses the Southern Fragment to construct a genocidal extermination weapon. \item \textbf{The Inquisitor's Iron Cage:} Infiltrating the capital, Eirik is ensnared in an anti-Aura runic cage constructed by the Inquisition. \item \textbf{Vanya's Consecrated Sacrifice:} Vanya braves anti-Uren wards that severely burn her flesh, sustains critical spear wounds, shatters the anti-Aura prison cage, and pulls Eirik to safety. \item \textbf{The Deepening Bond:} Tending to her wounds with soothing Ren, their mutual reliance evolves into deep personal affection and unbreakable devotion. In the Royal Forbidden Archives, Eirik uncovers unredacted pioneer records that confirm the atrocities and child exploitation depicted in the volcanic cave. \item \textbf{Climax of Act III:} Eirik and Vanya defeat Arch-Inquisitor Vael, dismantle the extermination weapon, reclaim the \textbf{Southern Fragment}, and advance Eirik's mastery to \textbf{Ren (Stage 3)}. \end{itemize} \subsection{Act IV: The Convergence (Venheilheim)} \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5cm] \item \textbf{Return to the Origin Island:} Eirik and Vanya return to Venheilheim carrying the Cradle Fragment, the Northern Fragment, and the Southern Fragment. \item \textbf{Reassembling the Primordial Orb:} At the Altar of the First Dawn, the three fragments are reunited upon the central dais. The Primordial Orb blazes with pure, uncorrupted Ren. \item \textbf{Dissolution of the Mark:} The restored Orb releases a global wave of Ren that permanently dissolves the hereditary \textbf{Mark of the Forsaken}. Worldwide, Uren physical mutations begin gradually receding toward their ancestral Human baseline. \item \textbf{Energy Coexistence:} Aura and Miasma do not vanish; their existing techniques remain functional as preparatory baselines, but the forgotten path to bridge into true Ren becomes accessible to all mortals once more. \item \textbf{The Outbreak of Conflict:} The sudden restoration triggers immediate ideological panic and military mobilization across both nations. \end{itemize} \subsection{Act V: Drown the Sea} \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5cm] \item \textbf{The Final Confrontation:} Warmongering factions from both Human and Uren armies converge on Venheilheim to seize the restored Orb for total racial dominance. \item \textbf{Fulfilling the Prophecy:} The resulting armed struggle causes catastrophic loss of life among the extremist leadership of both nations, fulfilling the line of the prophecy: ``To drown the sea''[cite: 2]. \item \textbf{The Sovereign Purge:} Eirik and Vanya take the field together, systematically executing the unyielding zealots on both sides to safeguard the surviving common folk and break the cycle of generational violence[cite: 3]. \end{itemize} \subsection{Epilogue} \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5cm] \item \textbf{The Sacred Union:} Eirik and Vanya marry at the Altar of the First Dawn, formalizing the union between their peoples[cite: 2, 3]. \item \textbf{Shared Haven:} Venheilheim becomes a shared sanctuary bridging the Sunlit Reaches and the Ashplains of Nul[cite: 2, 3]. \item \textbf{Open Academies:} Open academies are established across the realm to instruct both Humans and former Uren in the undivided art of Ren[cite: 2, 3]. \item \textbf{A New Dawn:} While centuries of grief and cultural prejudice do not dissolve overnight, the institutionalized, biological, and magical barriers that divided humanity are permanently dismantled[cite: 2, 3]. \end{itemize} \end{document} </pasted_content I compared your new document with the current `Venheilheim_Master_Story.md` and the game. I haven't changed anything yet. Below are the real discrepancies first, then the intentional changes. ## Discrepancies to resolve 1. **Eirik can't hold the disguise while unconscious.** Act I ends with Eirik "drifts unconscious". Act II then has him found "maintaining his crimson-skinned, horned Uren disguise". Act I also says the disguise needs "absolute, unbroken conscious concentration". One of these has to change. Easiest options: - he's half-conscious and clinging on, not unconscious; or - he comes to as the ship nears and puts the disguise on before they reach him. 2. **The volcanoes are in the wrong direction.** Your own geography puts "active volcanoes, magma fissures, and the Obsidian Spires in the west". Act II has Eirik and Vanya flee the Spires "eastward toward the Volcanoes". Either make it "inland" or "west", or move the volcano field to the east (Cinder Hold already sits in the ash-covered east). 3. **Malakor's arc never resolves.** He disappears after Act II's opening, and no act includes a confrontation with him or says what happens to him. The old Act II had Vanya leading Eirik to Malakor's citadel and revealing Malakor's link to the Northern Fragment. 4. **The Northern Fragment is never obtained.** Act III only covers the Southern Fragment, yet Act IV has them carrying all three. Act IV also says they carry the Cradle Fragment *to* Venheilheim, but it never left. It should read "carrying the Northern and Southern Fragments to the Cradle Fragment". 5. **Guard and parry are taught twice.** In Act I, the first combat teaches "light slashing chains, dodges, guards, parries, and heavy strikes", but Training stage 1 is "Guard and Parry" again. The old script and the game do it like this: - first fight: Slash and Dodge; - after the first Sentinel: Heavy; - in the Training Grounds: Guard and Parry. I'd keep that order. 6. **"Ren (Stage 3)" in Act III.** No stages 1 or 2 are defined anywhere. Either define the Ren stages or drop the number. 7. **Act V now contradicts the old ending.** The old script said "Eirik does not simply mass-kill ideological enemies". The new "Sovereign Purge" has Eirik and Vanya "systematically executing" the zealots on both sides. The new version is fine if that's what you intend, but it's a real change in Eirik's ending. 8. **Vanya's weapon doesn't match anywhere.** The new document gives her a single "curved obsidian blade". The spec and handoff say "twin curved blades", and the cast sheet says "Curved Obsidian Daggers". Pick one. 9. **The mist works differently.** The new document says the mist "turns back any ship whose crew lacks Ren". The old canon says ships get lost and "no one who enters returns". These are different mechanics. Pick one; "lost" fits the legend better. 10. **Miasma's origin is slightly inconsistent.** The new mythology says Miasma existed *before* the Mark (the fringe peoples' crude, unfiltered intake), but the energy table lists its circulation as "Mark-distorted". It should read something like "crude intake, locked by the Mark". ## Intentional changes (no conflict, but different from before) **Mythology** - **Aura is now ancient.** It used to be a crude method invented after Ren was lost. Now the pioneers created it as a preparation for Ren, and most people never went past it. A side effect: the relic's claim that "Venheilheim was a realm of Aura" is now a half-truth, which actually makes it a better lie. - **Miasma** is now the northern counterpart of Aura, another preparatory path, which the Mark froze in place. - **The first attack has a new motive.** Before, the pioneers experimented on the peripheral peoples *first*, and radicals later manipulated the children into a theft. Now the academies came first and the abuse happened inside them; the peripheral leaders raided to *protect* their children. That makes the Uren side far more sympathetic. - **The order after the first attack changed.** The academies closed and the Guardians were appointed *before* the Mark; previously the Mark came first. Both still happen after the first attack, so nothing breaks. - **New lore:** human bodies have weakened over the generations, so losing your Aura Core means being crippled. This fits Eirik well. - **The prophecy** is now also carved into the altar socket, as well as being spoken by the incarnation. **Act I** - **New item, the Resonance Fragment.** The incarnation gives Eirik a compass shard that glows near the Northern Fragment. It's not in the game yet. - **The incarnation now explicitly says** he was summoned by the bloodline failsafe. The old text kept her vaguer. - **The alcohol reason is now settled:** drink dulls his concentration. The old script left it pending, and the game's line ("Wine clouds the mind…") already matches. - **The ruins records are gone.** The new document drops "Ancient Ruins" and "Deeper Ruins", where murals show figures channelling energy without a Core. The game has these as lore spots. I'd keep them unless you want them cut. **Act II (fully rewritten; this replaces the old patrol-raid version)** - Vanya is disgraced for opposing the invasion, and sent home. - She rescues Eirik, who gives the alias "Torin". - Sea fights on the voyage; the crew grow jealous; he refuses all drink. - Arrival at the Obsidian Spires, where he searches the city with the Resonance Fragment. - Drunk Vanya in his quarters: the disguise breaks whether the player accepts or refuses the drink. - Her soldiers burst in and accuse them of treason, and the two escape by stable. - A playable ride; Eirik confesses he's King Eirik; she puts her blade to his throat. - The ground collapses and drops them into a cavern, where the engravings show the true history. - **Dropped from the old Act II:** the Uren families with meridian rot, and the inquisitorial patrol. **The true history now comes out earlier:** in Act II (the cave) and Act III (the Forbidden Archives), instead of Act IV. Act IV no longer has a history reveal. **Vael** is now "Arch-Inquisitor". The old note that Vael himself doesn't know the source is an Orb fragment is no longer stated. That isn't a contradiction, just missing. **The new document leaves out other old details:** - Malakor's ducal family, the books he burned, and the fact that he's wrong about the Orb; - the Hollow Shard's built-in instructions; - the meridian diagram; - the Act I rule that Miasma isn't explained. These are omissions rather than contradictions, so I'd keep them in the master file. ## Effect on the game - The relic pages, the seal, the disguise warning and the ship all already match. - The Resonance Fragment needs adding to the Cradle scene. - If you decide that Eirik is conscious at the wreck (point 1), the ending text changes slightly. Give me your calls on 1–10. I'll then merge this document into `Venheilheim_Master_Story.md`, keeping the omitted details, update the spec and handoff, and add the Resonance Fragment to the Cradle scene.

Response 741 wordsI've written the gorge into Act III (§14 of the master story) and updated the handoff. The register idea works…
I've written the gorge into Act III (§14 of the master story) and updated the handoff. The register idea works, with one change: since "Malakor" is the name everyone knows, the gate has to want a name nobody knows. So "Malakor" becomes the name he rules by, and the answer is his **given name**. He once signed it in the army muster rolls when he served, before he took his family's place. The character bible only gives him the one name, so I've used **"Kaedric"** as a placeholder; rename it freely. This also fits what we already have: his family has always hidden behind puppet Reys, so locking the vault with his own hidden name is in character. And it makes Vanya essential: Eirik could never open it alone. **What's in the gorge now** - **Malakor's house guard** holds it. They're loyal to him, not the army, and Vanya has never seen them on any muster. - **The gate:** Eirik guesses "Eirik of Solaris", then "Malakor". Each wrong answer sets off a trap. Then Vanya remembers a register entry with a ducal seal and speaks the name. **The traps.** Each one is also a beat between them. The tension stays unspoken: interrupted near-moments, and Eirik feeling guilty about Syra whenever he catches himself looking at her. 1. **The Watch Ledge:** they hide chest to chest in a crack barely wide enough for one while a patrol passes overhead. Neither moves for much longer than they need to. 2. **The Ward Stones:** runestones burn anyone carrying Miasma, so Vanya can't cross. Eirik can, because Ren isn't Miasma, and it's her first proof that he's something different. He has to carry her across, and they trade insults the whole way. 3. **The Shackle Gauntlet:** manacles chain them wrist to wrist, with swinging blades ahead. They start out pulling in opposite directions and end up moving in step without a word. They stay chained until they find a key. 4. **The Breath Vents:** sulphur gas. Vanya, used to thick Ashplains air, has to count Eirik's breaths close to his ear. It's the first time she's gentle with him. 5. **The Fall:** the bridge is cut and he catches her by the wrist over the drop. For a second it's a real choice: a Human king holding an Uren commander over a gorge. He pulls her up and she doesn't thank him, but from then on she calls him by his name. ## How they get back: suggestions **A. Malakor's own supply boat (my recommendation).** The gorge river runs out to a hidden cove on the eastern coast, where Malakor's people bring in supplies by boat. Here's the Ren gameplay I'd build. It follows spec §§8–12 and the lore that raw Ren can tear meridians that haven't been trained, and it keeps everything that already works. ## The idea in one line Ren isn't a list of spells. You steer it through Eirik's body, and wherever it goes, his next physical move becomes stronger. Moves you practise often enough happen on their own. ## 1. The resource: Strain instead of a mana bar The current "mind" bar works like mana, which the spec rules out. I'd replace it with **Strain**: - Ren itself never runs out. What limits Eirik is how much his untrained meridians can carry. - Each technique raises Strain, and Strain cools quickly when you stop using Ren. - If it fills up, his meridians seize: Eirik staggers and can't use Ren for about 4 seconds. - Training conditions the meridians, so each move strains him less. That way the training is how he grows stronger, not a bigger mana pool. - On the HUD, a small body icon shows white Ren running through it. It glows red as Strain rises. ## 2. Meridian View - **Controls:** hold the Ren button (or R on keyboard) to open it. The world fades and Eirik's body appears large in the centre, showing the 10 meridians, some fine minor ones, and Ren flowing as a white light. - **Steering:** the Ren light moves along a meridian until it reaches a junction. There, W/A/S/D (or the joystick on mobile) picks which way it goes next. The path it leaves behind is your route. - **Junctions:** - **Heart:** W goes up the Central Aortic, S goes down to the pelvis. - **Throat:** A takes the Left Arm, D the Right Arm, W the Carotids to the head. - **Pelvis:** A takes the Left Leg, D the Right Leg. - **Return paths:** the Superior Return, the Inferior Return and the Posterior (spine) carry Ren back to the heart. - **In combat,** time slows to about 20% instead of pausing, so routing Ren is a skill in itself. ## 3. The Aura failure (the opening moment in the ruins) This happens when Eirik first wakes. He reaches for Aura out of habit: 1. The view opens in old gold Aura colours. The player guides gold motes in through the skin, along the fine meridians, toward the Core. 2. Where the Core should be there's only a dark hole. The gold leaks out and disappears, and Eirik staggers. 3. Then a faint white current starts moving through his meridians on its own, with no Core involved. He shuts the view: *"No."* It takes about 30 seconds, and it teaches the controls through the story instead of through text. ## 4. The four training exercises (Training Grounds) These replace the inscription lessons. The inscriptions stay as lore. | Exercise | What you do | What it unlocks | |---|---|---| | **Circle** | Steer Ren around the full loop (heart → head → spine → legs → heart) and press each junction in time. Three unbroken laps. | Ren circulation and the Strain HUD | | **Branch** | Body regions light up. Send Ren into each one and back without breaking the loop. | Manual Ren in combat (section 5) | | **Pulse** | Hold to pack Ren into one region and stop inside a target zone. Overshoot and the meridian strains. Then pulse your arm and break a stone block with one slash. | Reinforced Slash (white veins), **Ren Blade**, **Ren Wave** (a long two-arm pulse) | | **Shape** | Hold Ren in your forearm until the skin hardens to stone-grey, then take a Sentinel's blow on it. | **Ren Body**. It also sets up the incarnation's disguise lesson | ## 5. Ren in combat **Stage 1, manual routing.** Hold Ren, steer a route, then release. Your next physical move becomes a technique: - **Right Arm + Slash:** a reinforced slash with white veins up the arm, more damage, and the enemy staggers. - **Legs + Dodge:** a longer Ren step with a longer window where he can't be hit. - **Carotids:** brief Ren sight that makes enemy attack wind-ups obvious. This also ties into seeing through the mist on the voyage. - **Posterior + Guard:** an unbreakable block that knocks the attacker back. - **Timing:** releasing right as the move connects gives a "perfect" bonus. This is the spec's formula: **Physical Action + Ren Flow + Timing = Technique**. **Stage 2, mastery.** Every action-plus-route pair counts its clean uses. After about 12, it becomes **Mastered** and can be set to fire automatically during that move, still costing Strain. Act I allows two of these slots. - A **Techniques** page in the pause menu lists what you've recorded and mastered. - Underneath, a technique is stored as `{action, route, timing}`, which supports the spec's future player-made techniques. **Buttons.** Ren Blade, Body and Wave keep their existing buttons (mobile needs them). They count as mastered techniques, so they're earned through the exercises instead of handed out. ## 6. Uren disguise (spec §12) After the incarnation's lesson it becomes a held ability, built on Shape: crimson skin, horns and collarbone markings. Strain rises steadily while it's active. Letting go, or filling Strain, ends it. The transformation frames already exist. ## 7. Art I'd need from you - A front-view **body figure** of Eirik for the Meridian View, dim and about 120 px tall. I'd draw a placeholder silhouette until it arrives. - The white veins, stone skin and Ren light I can draw in code. ## Build order (each step ships as its own version) 1. Meridian View and the Aura failure scene. 2. Strain replaces the mind bar; Circle and Branch. 3. Pulse and Shape; the veined Slash; the three techniques unlocked through the exercises. 4. Manual combat routing, mastery and the Techniques page. 5. The disguise as an ability. Old saves keep whatever they've already learned. Every step comes with tests and screenshots, as usual. I'd ask you to confirm one choice: **Strain** (Ren is unlimited and the body is the limit, which fits the lore) or keeping a **Ren pool** that drains (closer to the spec's literal wording "continuous Ren consumption"). I recommend Strain. Unless you'd rather keep a pool, I'll start on step 1 next.

For this project I'd keep the code on GitHub, but the size problem you're probably running into is real and needs fixing either way. **What I see in the repo:** - It points at `github.com/Dasa108/Venheilheim`. - The `.git` folder is **30 GB**. The working files are only about 2 GB: `game/` 551 MB, `art_sources/` 487 MB, `production_vault/` 181 MB, `build/` 950 MB. - So almost all of the size is history, the many saved versions of PNGs and other binaries from earlier commits. - GitHub rejects any single file over 100 MB and doesn't cope well with repos over a few GB. Pushing this one as it stands will fail or crawl. **Why not Hugging Face for the project itself:** - It's built for AI models and datasets. It handles big files well, but it has nothing like GitHub's Actions for automated builds and tests. - Its issue tracking is limited to discussions. - Godot tooling, and anyone you'd collaborate with, expect GitHub. - Where it could fit is as a storage bucket for large art sources or built APKs, alongside GitHub. **What I'd do:** 1. Keep the code and the game on GitHub. 2. Move images, audio, `.apk` and `.x86_64` files to Git LFS, which GitHub supports. Stop tracking `build/`; it's regenerated on every export anyway. 3. Rewrite the history so the old binary versions drop out of `.git`. That should take it from 30 GB to a few GB. This is a one-time, irreversible change to history, so I'd do it only with your go-ahead. 4. For sharing playable builds, use itch.io (free, made for games) or GitHub Releases rather than committing the files. Want me to set up LFS and clean the history? I'd first make a backup copy of the repo, show you what would be removed, and wait for your OK before pushing.

To attach a display, the process that runs the game needs access to the desktop session’s display socket and authorization. For X11, that means DISPLAY (often :0), the matching XAUTHORITY file, and /tmp/.X11-unix; for Wayland, it needs WAYLAND_DISPLAY, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, and that socket. The environment hosting this workspace must pass those through when starting the session. The pieces that need to be passed through are all present: - **X11 (through XWayland):** `DISPLAY=:0`, the authorisation file `/run/user/1000/.mutter-Xwaylandauth.ETIWW3`, and the socket `/tmp/.X11-unix/X0`. - **Wayland:** `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000`, with the socket `/run/user/1000/wayland-0`. Godot opens its window through X11 by default, so the X11 values above are the ones that matter. They're the same ones my game windows use. **Two things to know before you hand them over:** - **The authorisation file name changes every time you log in.** The `ETIWW3` part is new each session, so whatever you're setting up should read `$XAUTHORITY` when it starts rather than use that exact path. - **Anything given these values can open windows on your desktop and read its input.** Pass them only to a tool you trust, and only for this login session.

Bugs fixed - Switching between two protected apps could stop the timer. Going from Chrome straight into WhatsApp could leave the ticker dead, so the second app had no countdown and no penalty check. - A penalty that started while its app was open didn't lock the app until you left it. It now locks within a second. - Penalty rechecks fired at the wrong time. They ran on a fixed timer even while the penalty was paused (Vault at zero), which could pile up penalties, and they were lost on reboot. They now run when the penalty countdown actually reaches zero. - Rerolls were used up even when no penalty could apply (no protected apps, or 0 penalty minutes). - Late completions still paid the full reward. The spec says only on-time tasks earn minutes, so a late completion now earns nothing but still stops further penalties. - Reset gave you a fresh 30 minutes, which made it an easy way to refill the Vault. Reset now keeps today's allowance markers, so your balance stays at zero until tomorrow's allowance. - The Vault screen didn't scroll. "Today", the metrics and Reset were cut off at the bottom and couldn't be reached. I found this on your phone. - Export shared plain text that Import couldn't open. It now saves a real .json file, and Import checks priority and value ranges. - Task reminders had no date, so a reminder could land after the deadline, and you could set a deadline in the past. - Returning to the app reset the tab and the task form. - The usage cache never worked, so every second hit the database. Spec features that were missing and are now built - Sorting tasks by Due date, Priority or Eisenhower. - Picking a priority fills in its default reward (30/20/10 minutes). - A 120-character limit on task titles. - The block screen now shows the app's name and a "Next up" card with your most important open task. - App names instead of package names throughout. Still open (listed in spec §9, not fixed) These are design questions, so I left them for you to decide: - The daily unlock rule (FR-3.8) is easy to game. Completing one trivial task turns off all limits for the rest of the day. Your phone shows 21 minutes earned against 274 spent today with no open tasks, so it may already be happening. - You set your own reward amounts, rerolls can be farmed using far-off deadlines, and deadlines can be pushed back as often as you like. - Restoring an old backup or resetting can get you out of a penalty. - FR-3.2 (detecting attempts to disable FocusBank) isn't built. - Two permissions are declared but unused: SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS. - The database still runs on the main thread. Logo The new icon is a vault door (lime ring with bolts on dark navy) with a teal-to-amber time arc and a check mark in the middle. It stays clear at small sizes, adapts to themed icons on Android 13+, and the notifications now use a matching small icon instead of Android's generic lock and alarm icons. The icon files are the four drawables in res/drawable/. Docs - Learning-lab HTML: - Your new logo is in the header. - A new "9. Spec Audit" tab lists everything fixed and still open. - The simulator can now miss a deadline and show how the penalty pauses and rechecks. - Two new quiz questions, and the score percentages now work for any number of questions. - I corrected code samples that didn't match the real code. - The "Try Live Simulator" button did nothing and now works. - Spec: bumped to 1.2.0, with a new "Known Gaps" section (§9) and fixes to sections that contradicted the code. - decisions.md: it was empty even though the HTML links to it. Penalty rule A penalty now only counts down while you're spending Vault time in a different protected app. The penalized app stays locked the whole time. For example, with 60 minutes in the Vault and a 20-minute penalty on Instagram, 20 minutes of YouTube serves the penalty and leaves 40 minutes in the Vault. These don't count, so the penalty just waits: - The phone sitting idle, the home screen, or a locked or off screen. - An empty Vault. - Time from an app's own daily allowance, since it isn't Vault time. - Free use under the "all tasks done" daily unlock, since that costs nothing. When the penalty is fully served, the task is checked again as before. Tests (19 → 66) To make the blocking service testable, I moved its rules into a separate class, EnforcementEngine. It runs on one 1-second tick instead of the two separate timer loops that caused the 1.2 bug. The service is now just the Android wrapper around it. - Storage (19 tests): daily and extra allowance, rewards and late completions, rerolls, Vault charging, penalties, per-app allowance, the screen-free goal, backup and restore, reset, and migrating old tasks. - Blocking (22 tests), driven by a fake phone: - charging per second, blocking on an empty Vault, and penalty locks; - keyboards and phone-maker system apps being ignored, and screen-off or lock pauses; - the daily unlock and screen-free goal; - the new penalty rule, and the old switch-apps bug from 1.2. - Penalty recheck (6 tests): a new penalty if the task is still open, rerolls, and alarm scheduling. Raising it isn't a one-line change: newer Android versions force the app to draw edge to edge, so the screens need adjusting and retesting on your phone. 2. No consent screen before the Accessibility request. The "Enable blocking" button jumps straight to Android's Accessibility settings. For apps that use the Accessibility API for something other than helping disabled users, Play requires an in-app screen first. It has to say what's monitored and why, and you have to tap to agree. Play rejects apps without this. 3. QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES is probably unnecessary. Play restricts this permission to a few kinds of apps, and an app blocker may not qualify. FocusBank only needs apps that appear in the launcher, and a small manifest entry can list those without the permission. Removing it avoids a likely rejection. 4. Release signing isn't set up. There's no signing config yet. You create the keystore yourself and keep it out of git; I can wire Gradle to read it from a local file. Shrinking (R8) is also off, which is allowed, but the spec says it should be on. Things only you can do 5. Privacy policy: you need a public URL. Play Console forms: Data safety, the Accessibility API declaration (they usually want a short video of the feature), the foreground-service "special use" justification, content rating, and store images (512px icon, feature graphic, screenshots). 7. The verse texts in the app. Those English translations come from prabhupadabooks.com and are almost certainly copyrighted by their publisher. Showing them in a published app likely needs permission. Otherwise, switch to a translation you're allowed to use, or show only the verse reference and the link. 8. What I meant by "a closed test with testers" Google Play has testing tracks where you publish the app to a limited group before releasing it to everyone. A closed test is one of these: only people you invite can install it, through a private Play Store link. For you it's probably mandatory, not optional. If your developer account is a personal account created after November 2023, Google won't let you publish to production until you've run a closed test. The rule as I last knew it: - At least 12 testers opted in (it used to be 20). - They stay opted in for 14 days in a row. - Then you apply for production access in the Play Console. Google asks what you tested and what feedback you got. Organization accounts (registered as a company) are exempt. Google has changed these numbers before, so check the Dashboard in your Play Console, which shows the current requirement for your account. How it works in practice: 1. Upload the signed app bundle to the Closed testing track. 2. Add testers by email address or a Google Group. 3. Share the opt-in link. Each tester taps it, accepts, and installs FocusBank from the Play Store. 4. Wait the 14 days. Testers don't need to use the app every day, but they must stay opted in, and some real use helps when you apply. 5. Apply for production access and answer Google's questions. Tips for FocusBank: - Recruit testers with different phone brands (Samsung, Pixel, Xiaomi), since blocking behaves differently across manufacturers. - Ask them to actually enable blocking, miss a deadline, and restart their phone. - Start as early as you can: the 14 days can run while you finish the privacy policy and store listing. The first step is still the signed release build, which needs your keystore. Want me to set up the Gradle signing config so you only have to create the key? ✻ Crunched for 19s · done Wednesday, Sep 30, 1:38 AM

This puts the key file outside the repository, next to your AIDS folder. 2. Copy keystore.properties.example to keystore.properties and fill in your two passwords. 3. Back up the .jks file and the passwords somewhere safe, such as a password manager. If you lose them, Google Play can reset the key, but only through their support team. 4. Build the upload file with ./gradlew bundleRelease. It ends up at app/build/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab. 5. The first time you upload to the Play Console, accept Play App Signing. Google then keeps the real signing key, and yours is just the upload key. Worth knowing: code shrinking (R8) is still off. That's allowed; it just makes the download a bit bigger. Ran 1 shell command, wrote 1 memory (ctrl+o to expand) ● Before I answer the UPI question, let me check exactly what FocusBank's Accessibility service currently asks Android for: Searched for 1 pattern (ctrl+o to expand) ● This is the UPI apps protecting themselves, not a FocusBank bug. Fraud apps on Android often use the Accessibility API to read the screen and steal payment details. So Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm and many bank apps refuse or block payments while an Accessibility service they don't trust is switched on. FocusBank's service asks for the riskiest-looking ability: reading window content (canRetrieveWindowContent), which it uses only to read the on-screen app's package name. It's also installed outside the Play Store, which some UPI apps treat as a red flag on its own. Telling FocusBank to ignore the UPI apps won't help. They check whether the service is switched on, not what it watches. Here's what can work: 1. A "Pause for a payment" button (recommended, works with every UPI app). Tapping it switches FocusBank's service off itself, using Android's disableSelf(), so your payment goes through. A few minutes later a notification reminds you to turn blocking back on, with a button straight to the right Settings screen. One limitation: Android lets an app switch its own Accessibility service off but never back on, so turning it back on is always a couple of taps in Settings. This adds no new loophole, since you can already switch it off in Settings. 2. Make the service look less risky (might help, not guaranteed). I can drop the window-reading ability and rely only on app-switch events. Some UPI apps only object to services that can read the screen, so this may be enough for yours, but each app has its own secret rules, so I can't promise it. The cost is that the app-detection fallback goes away, so the original Vivo "missing seconds" problem could partly come back. 3. Publish on the Play Store later. A few UPI apps only distrust services installed from outside the Play Store. That's for when you publish. My suggestion is option 1 now, since it's reliable. We could also try option 2 as an experiment you test with your UPI app; it's easy to undo. Status of the other work: the Plan task type and the review fixes are built into version 1.6.0, installed on your phone, and all 80 tests pass. The database upgrade worked on your real data: your 1 task is still there and is now a commitment. None of this is committed to git yet, and the spec and HTML still need updating. can we not exclude certain apps from the checking??
Response 332 wordsPartly. Android does let an Accessibility service limit which apps it receives
● Partly. Android does let an Accessibility service limit which apps it receives events from (android:packageNames). It's an "only these apps" list rather than an exclude list, but it amounts to the same thing. FocusBank could watch only: - your protected apps, - your home launcher, so it knows when you leave, - itself. It can update that list on the fly whenever you protect or unprotect an app. UPI and bank apps would then not be on the list, so FocusBank would get no events from them at all. Whether it fixes payments depends on how your UPI app checks: - Some apps only object to services that can see them. Restricting the list should fix those. - Some block payment whenever any non-system Accessibility service is switched on, whatever it watches. For those, nothing except turning FocusBank off helps. That's what the "Pause for a payment" button would be for. Each UPI app keeps its rule secret, so the only way to know is to try it with yours. What it costs FocusBank: - Jumping straight from a protected app to an unprotected one without passing the home screen (via recents, say) sends no event. The 1-second check would still catch it, so tracking stays correct. - That 1-second check still has the ability to read whichever window is in front, and a strict UPI app might object to that ability alone. If so, the next step is dropping it, which brings back some of the old Vivo detection risk. My suggestion: build the include list now, plus the "Pause for a payment" button as a guaranteed fallback. You then try a small payment, say ₹1, in your UPI app to see whether it's enough. It's all easy to undo if it causes problems. Should I go ahead? And which UPI app are you using (GPay, PhonePe, Paytm, a bank app)? That tells me what to watch out for. ✻ Crunched for 19s · done Monday, Oct 5, 11:00 PM
